next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a China-linked group known by many names, tied to HyperBro and other tools
next.in_short: Threat Group-3390 goes by many names, including Emissary Panda and APT27. The cards on file are thin. One report names the group among users of Scanbox; another lists HyperBro samples.

sentences.t: MITRE tracks the group as Threat Group-3390.
Its aliases include Earth Smilodon, TG-3390, Emissary Panda, BRONZE UNION, APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse and Linen Typhoon.
Recorded Future's Insikt Group lists LuckyMouse (TG-3390, Emissary Panda, Bronze Union) among actors that have historically used the Scanbox framework.
The same report says Scanbox has been used before against persecuted minority groups, such as the Uighurs.

The report ties the March 2019 Scanbox campaigns to other targets, a Pakistani government passport tracking page and a spoofed Central Tibetan Administration site. It does not name this group as behind them.
MITRE's record lists many tools for the group. They include PlugX, HyperBro, China Chopper, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, gh0st RAT, SysUpdate and RCSession.
Scanbox is a reconnaissance framework written in JavaScript and PHP. It can log keystrokes.
Insikt Group says attackers using Scanbox likely aim to profile visitors' devices so they can carry out follow-on intrusions.
A threat report titled 'Iron Tiger Compromises Chat Application Mimi, Targets Windows, Mac, and Linux Users' is mostly a list of indicators of compromise.
It lists file hashes for HyperBro samples on Windows and Rshell samples on Linux and Mac OS.
The page gives no account of who was targeted, where, or when the activity took place.
Defenders who want more detail should look for fuller reporting, since the material here is limited.
